name: Expected Credit Loss
description: Gives the expected loss on a credit exposure: PD × LGD × EAD (Basel and IFRS 9).
notes: 2 % PD, 45 % LGD on 1,000,000 gives an expected loss of 9,000.

name: Net Interest Margin
description: Divides net interest income by average interest-earning assets.
notes: The core profitability measure for lenders.

name: Risk-Weighted Assets
description: Multiplies each exposure by its regulatory risk weight and adds them up (Basel standardised approach).
notes: Capital ratios are measured against this total.

name: Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio
description: Divides a bank's highest-quality capital by its risk-weighted assets.
notes: Basel III minimum 4.5 % plus a 2.5 % conservation buffer, and more for systemically important banks.

name: Leverage Ratio (Basel III)
description: Divides Tier 1 capital by total (not risk-weighted) exposure, a backstop to risk-based ratios.
notes: The Basel minimum is 3 %.

name: Liquidity Coverage Ratio
description: Divides high-quality liquid assets by stressed net cash outflows over 30 days; must be at least 100 %.
notes: Introduced by Basel III after the 2008 crisis.

name: Loan-to-Deposit Ratio
description: Divides loans by deposits; above 100 % the bank relies on wholesale funding.
notes: Too low can mean idle funds; too high, liquidity risk.

name: Cost-to-Income Ratio
description: Divides operating costs by operating income; lower is more efficient.
notes: Also called the efficiency ratio.

name: Non-Performing Loan Ratio
description: Gives the share of loans that are in default or close to it.
notes: Above about 5 % signals asset-quality problems.

name: Basel IRB Capital Requirement (Corporate)
description: Gives capital per unit of exposure under the Basel internal-ratings-based formula for corporate loans (Vasicek one-factor model at 99.9 %, with maturity adjustment).
notes: Risk-weighted assets are K × 12.5 × EAD. PD 1 % and LGD 45 % give K ≈ 0.0739.

name: Repricing Gap Effect on Net Interest Income
description: Estimates the change in a bank's net interest income over the gap period when rates move by Δr.
notes: A negative gap (more liabilities repricing) loses when rates rise.

name: Duration Gap
description: Gives the duration gap D_A − (L/A)·D_L, which drives how equity value reacts to interest rates.
notes: Change in equity ≈ −gap × assets × Δr/(1 + r).

name: Economic Value of Equity Change
expression: -(da - dl * liab / assets) * assets * dr / (1 + r)
description: Estimates the change in a bank's economic value of equity for a parallel rate shock (IRRBB).
notes: Supervisors look at shocks of ±200 basis points.

name: Provision Coverage Ratio
description: Divides loan-loss reserves by non-performing loans.
notes: Shows how much of the bad loans is already provided for.

name: Cumulative Default Probability over n Years
description: Gives the chance of default at some point within n years from a constant annual default probability.
notes: 2 % a year compounds to about 9.6 % over five years.

name: Annual Default Probability from Cumulative
description: Converts a cumulative default probability over n years into the equivalent constant annual rate.
notes: Useful for reading rating-agency default studies.

name: Vasicek Portfolio Loss Quantile
description: Gives the default rate of a large, granular loan portfolio that is exceeded only with probability 1 − q, under the Vasicek one-factor model.
notes: The core of the Basel IRB formula; multiply by LGD for the loss rate.

name: Bank Z-Score (Distance to Insolvency)
description: Gives how many standard deviations ROA would have to fall to wipe out a bank's equity.
notes: Widely used in banking research as a stability measure.

name: Net Stable Funding Ratio
description: Compares a bank's stable funding with what its assets require over one year; Basel III requires at least 100 %.
notes: Complements the short-term Liquidity Coverage Ratio.

name: Unexpected Loss of a Single Exposure
expression: ead * sqrt(pd * sdl^2 + lgd^2 * pd * (1 - pd))
description: Computes the unexpected loss (standard deviation of the loss) of one loan when both default and the loss given default are uncertain.
notes: Default and LGD are assumed independent. For a fixed LGD, set its standard deviation to 0.

name: Total Capital Ratio
description: Computes a bank's total capital ratio, Tier 1 plus Tier 2 capital divided by risk-weighted assets.
notes: Basel III sets a minimum of 8 % before buffers; national rules add further requirements.

name: Texas Ratio
description: Computes the Texas ratio, bad assets divided by the capital and reserves available to absorb them.
notes: Non-performing assets usually include repossessed property. Values near or above 100 % signal a bank in serious difficulty.

name: Lifetime Expected Credit Loss from Marginal PDs
expression: sum(k, 1, len(mpd), at(mpd, k) * lgd * ead / (1 + eir)^k)

variables.label: Marginal default probability for each year

description: Computes a lifetime expected credit loss as the sum of each year's default probability × LGD × exposure, discounted at the effective interest rate (as in IFRS 9).
notes: The exposure is held constant here; for an amortising loan use a different exposure for each year.

name: Conditional (Forward) Default Probability

variables.label: Cumulative PD to the start of the period
Cumulative PD to the end of the period

description: Computes the probability of default in a period for a borrower that has survived to its start, from two cumulative default probabilities.
notes: The difference cum2 − cum1 alone is the unconditional (marginal) probability.

name: Constant Hazard Rate from a Cumulative PD
description: Computes the constant default intensity (hazard rate) that produces a given cumulative default probability over a horizon.
notes: Assumes defaults arrive at a constant rate, so the survival probability is e^(−λt).

name: Loss Given Default from Collateral
description: Computes the loss given default as the part of the exposure not covered by the collateral after a haircut.
notes: The haircut covers the fall in value and the cost of selling the collateral. Recovery costs and time value are otherwise ignored.

name: Net Charge-off Rate
description: Computes the net charge-off rate, loans written off less later recoveries, as a share of average loans.
notes: For a quarter, multiply by 4 to state an annual rate.

name: Collateral Coverage Ratio
description: Computes how much of a loan is covered by its collateral after a haircut.
notes: Below 100 % part of the loan is unsecured. The haircut depends on the type of collateral and the lender's policy.
